drafted_from: workflow:tell-me-when-something-changes's own file, tools/workflows/recipes/tell-me-when-something-changes.json, and the store matrix of 2026-11-18 (each store's own change_feed)
start_here: Say to your AI: "Run workflow:tell-me-when-something-changes with store {\"where\": \"notes folder on my computer\", \"language\": \"markdown files\"} and watch [\"lesson-requests\"]." From then on, each lesson request added there is told once, and the workflows that follow it start.
no_lists_because: It keeps nothing in lists: the store tells its own changes as facts, and a store that cannot tell keeps its own last read beside the watched things.
instructions: 1. Keep the store's login in your vault under a name you choose, and say where the store is, how it is spoken to, and which things to watch.
2. Say "Run workflow:tell-me-when-something-changes" with store and watch.
3. The first run finds the store's own way of telling (or makes a scheduled read and compare), makes it once, and proves it on the example changes below: each must give its expected fact once.
4. Turn on workflow:route-each-row-change's wake a-row-changed: each fact then starts every workflow whose conditions follow that change.

examples.change: the same entry's topic changed to "moon tides"
an entry whose text is 5,000 characters added

expected_fact.after: left out: it does not fit; a run reads it by key

worked_examples.title: A folder of markdown files tells each lesson request added
worked_examples.ask: Tell my workflows whenever I add a lesson request to my notes folder.
worked_examples.given: The look step found that a folder of files has no way of its own to tell a change.
worked_examples.hands_back: made ["a due-time wake every 60 seconds that reads lesson-requests, compares it with the last read kept beside it, and tells each added, changed or removed file as row-changes"]; the prove step then passes all five examples.

example_renderings.for: a Postgres database made by workflow:make-a-database-for-each-pursuit
example_renderings.what: The Postgres leaf the noticer uses, read as one example rendering of this workflow for a Postgres store: it reads the database's own change table in commit order and tells each change as something-changed. It is one person's own choice for a Postgres store, not a shared default; the shared leaf stays where it is, and any store can be rendered from this kit's intent and examples.
